record.paper_title: Causal Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can model-based reinforcement learning, in which a learned model is used for planning, be merged with causal discovery, in which causal structure is learned from data, so that reinforcement-learning or multi-agent reinforcement-learning systems can learn a causal model and then use that model for identification and planning?

evidence.quote: The problem posed by causal discovery is related to problems posed in RL literature, where model-based approaches often propose learning a model before using it for planning (Moerland et al., 2020). Further, RL methods have been applied for causal structure learning (Zhu et al., 2019). The authors believe there is great opportunity for merging model-based RL and causal discovery methods.
As in model-based (MA)RL, it may be of interest to ﬁrst learn a causal model and then use it for identiﬁcation and planning. Recent causality literature usually frames this as causal discovery.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a (multi-agent) reinforcement-learning setting in which one or more agents interact with an unknown environment by choosing actions, receiving rewards, and observing state transitions generated by some underlying structural causal model. In model-based reinforcement learning, the agent first estimates a predictive model of the environment dynamics and reward, and then uses this model for planning (e.g., via simulation, value iteration, or trajectory optimization). In causal discovery, one instead seeks to learn, from observational and interventional data, a causal structure — typically encoded as a directed acyclic graph together with structural equations or conditional distributions over variables (states, actions, rewards, latent confounders) — that captures the data-generating mechanism and supports interventional and counterfactual queries.

Develop a unified framework and algorithm that integrates these two paradigms for (multi-agent) reinforcement learning. Specifically, provide:

1. A formal definition of a learned object — a causal world model — that combines a structural causal model over the relevant state, action, reward, and (possibly) latent confounder variables with the predictive role of a model-based RL transition/reward model.

2. A learning procedure that uses the data collected by the agent(s) (including interventional data arising from the agents' own actions) to jointly perform causal discovery and dynamics/reward estimation, with explicit treatment of identifiability of the causal structure from such data.

3. A planning procedure that uses the learned causal model to compute policies, taking advantage of causal identification (e.g., do-calculus, counterfactual reasoning) for credit assignment, transfer, and coordination among multiple agents.

4. Theoretical guarantees on sample complexity, identifiability, and convergence (or regret) of the combined causal-discovery-plus-model-based-RL procedure in the single-agent and multi-agent settings.

The problem is to construct such a framework and to characterize the conditions under which the causal model is identifiable from the agents' interaction data and yields provably improved planning compared to non-causal model-based reinforcement learning.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open research direction at the intersection of model-based reinforcement learning and causal discovery. Numerous recent works (e.g., on causal world models, causal MBRL, and using RL for causal structure learning) make partial progress, but no unified framework with general identifiability and planning guarantees — particularly in the multi-agent setting — has been established. The problem is best characterized as open.

status_evidence.title: Causal Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys integration of causal inference with RL and highlights open problems including learning causal world models for planning.
status_evidence.claim: Integration of causal discovery and model-based RL remains an active, open research area.

status_evidence.title: Causal Discovery with Reinforcement Learning (Zhu et al., 2019)
status_evidence.snippet: Uses RL to search over DAG structures for causal discovery; does not provide a unified causal model-based RL framework with planning guarantees.
status_evidence.claim: Existing works address one direction (RL for causal discovery) but not the full unification.
